observation.visible_scene: A person's hand (thumb and finger visible at the lower-left edge) holds a burning sparkler by its bare wire handle against an out-of-focus outdoor background of a green grassy field and a line of dark trees. The sparkler's coated tip burns as a bright white-yellow point near the center of the frame, continuously throwing off thin orange sparks and streaks. The hand and stick remain in roughly the same position throughout, with the glowing tip staying near the image center.
visible_changes: The overall tilt/orientation of the sparkler stick shifts gradually through the segment: early frames show the coated end angled up-right with a long horizontal spark streak to the right; mid frames (around t=0.20-0.80) show a more upright, fan-like spark pattern; later frames (t=0.87 onward) show the coated end pointing more horizontally to the right with dense radiating bursts.

The spark pattern is highly variable and non-repeating frame to frame: radiating lines, isolated starburst 'explosions' away from the tip (e.g., a separated starburst at left in t=0.87-1.13, top-left in t=1.20-1.47), and short falling streaks below the tip (visible in t=2.20-2.67) appear and disappear.
The brightness and spread of the central glow fluctuate, becoming a very dense bright cluster in t=1.53-2.13 and a slightly sparser spray in t=2.20-2.47.

The background (grass horizon and trees) and the hand's grip position stay essentially fixed, indicating the changes are in the sparkler's emission and slight stick angle rather than large scene movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the sparkler was lit and whether the burning will continue past the last frame (the segment ends mid-burn).
What hand/arm motion, if any, produces the small changes in stick tilt, since only the fingertips are visible.
The full extent of spark fall or the eventual end of the sparkler's active coating.
uncertain_details: Whether the slight apparent shift of the burning tip and stick angle is hand movement or small camera/handheld jitter; the background looks stable but camera motion cannot be fully ruled out.
Exact cause of individual spark streaks and starbursts (not observable, only their appearance).
Whether the coated portion of the sparkler is shortening over the segment; this is not clearly resolvable from the frames.
